First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}=\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}
$$

Next, we can further simplify our expression by factoring it as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1}{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)^{2}} & =\frac{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)(\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1)}{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)}(\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1)}{\cancel{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)}(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}=\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1}.
$$
